title: NeuroEdge Error v1
description: A serialised NeuroEdge diagnostic: the mandatory three parts (where, why, how; FR-DX-04) and a stable code, as `NeuroEdgeError.as_dict()` returns it and as Studio and the sim page report it under `error`. `code` is a pattern, not an enum: the codes that exist, their classes and their status are in error-codes.v1.json, which validates against `#/$defs/catalog`. The looser error bodies of the Studio API (docs/spec/studio.md §8) are that API's own contract, not this schema. Receivers must not branch on a `general` code (NE0000, NE2000).

code.description: Stable machine-readable identifier. Never reused for another meaning.

where.description: The precise location: a file path, a gate URI, a criterion name, a source line.

why.description: What rule was broken, quoting the offending and expected values.

how.description: A concrete next action the reader can take.

principle.description: NE2003: the Appendix B.5 principle that was violated, as a string.

reason.description: NE1002 and NE1003: why the command was refused. Open string.

catalog.description: The shape of error-codes.v1.json: the catalogue of every NE code.

code.description: Unique in the catalogue and never reused.

name.description: The public class in neuroedge.errors (a reserved code: the class it will have).

parent.description: Name of the parent class in the catalogue; null for the root.

status.description: stable: the class exists. reserved: the code is held for a class that does not exist yet.

fields.description: Keys `as_dict()` adds to the four common ones.

also_a.description: Other Python classes the error also is (only a Python SDK needs this).

general.description: An unclassified code: a receiver must not branch on it.

rfc.description: The RFC that added the code, when one did.
